text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Man killed, another injured in fall. They were working on a new building block when a plank collapsed.

- Mid-Med bank holds annual general meeting. Financial consultant Alfred Misfsud to become new chairman. The government owns two-thirds of Mid-Med, which a few weeks ago announced a pre-tax profit of Lm12.73 million (about $35 million.)

- Court starts rehearing of inquiry into tanker explosion. The Libyan tanker Um el Faroud exploded at Malta drydocks in February two years ago, killing nine dockyards workers. The first inquiry had found Malta drydocks working practices, mostly to blame for the incident, caused by an accumulation of gases in a tank.

- Possible double spending in new hospital project, report shows. The report, drawn up by an auditor, was commissioned by the government, which is looking into the $120 million hospital project started by the previous government. The project is still in its early stages and the government is being pressed to decide whether it will go ahead with it. The report found that "there seemed to be no clear idea over funding".
- Air Malta fares up by three percent because of fuel surcharge.
